text:
Tage Thompson is second in the league in wins added by goals, with 13 goals in 21 games, and the Sabres keep losing anyway: one win in their last six. After a 4-3 loss in Philadelphia the club's video headline quoted him on needing "desperation and urgency," and Heavy.com had him calling out a "troubling pattern" after a lopsided loss to Tampa Bay.

He has 85 shots in 21 games and 9.8 expected goals. The goals are a bit ahead of that, though his 15% shooting matches last season, so most of the gap is sheer volume rather than a fluky finishing rate. Our range for his season is 36 to 53 goals.

The issue is around him. Buffalo has taken about 50% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 93rd percentile last season and his value at 1.4 wins above replacement, modest for a 40-goal shooter. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he lives in the right places (7.4 chances per 60 from in front of the net, 93rd percentile). He's doing his job; the question is whether anyone else's line can tilt the ice.
headline: Thompson's goals can't fix Buffalo alone
